content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Please review these screenshots illustrating how to create a UDF in [product_name] [version_no]. Regards,
Great work [user_name]! There is an alternative way to create a UDF. Check the attached images. After image 2, follow steps 3 to 7 provided by [user_name]. Regards,

Hi all, While testing the UDF example, I noticed that if you design a UDF block using an AND function and connect four inputs initially, you must always use all four inputs when calling the block in another project. Using fewer inputs results in non-functional logic. Regards,
I have finished all the steps but cannot find the UDF in my new FDB project. Is it necessary to save the UDF in a specific folder?
Hello, After you save the UDF, go to Options, select UDF, and then add your UDF. It should now appear in your block list. Regards,
A new question posted by [user_name] was separated into a new thread titled 'Created a UDF but it is Greyed out when trying to use it in the Circuit Diagram.' Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Members are exchanging different methods and troubleshooting advice for building and managing User Defined Functions (UDFs) within [product_name] [version_no]. Users face issues with mandatory input requirements during UDF definition and with locating or accessing UDFs in new projects. This indicates that the software’s workflow and configuration procedures may lack clarity or transparency.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the process of creating and integrating UDFs to be straightforward, adaptable, and user-friendly. They would like the ability to reuse UDFs and manage input quantities flexibly across different projects, minimizing rigid constraints.
